We can perform polynomial long division:
$$n^3 = n(n^2 - n + 1) + n^2 - n,$$
so
$$\frac{n^3}{n^2 - n + 1} = n + \frac{n^2 - n}{n^2 - n + 1}.$$
Since $n \ge 3$ (as $k \ge 1$, and $n=5$ corresponds to $k=2$), we have $0 < n^2 - n < n^2 - n + 1$.
Thus $0 < \frac{n^2 - n}{n^2 - n + 1} < 1$.
Therefore, $\left\lfloor \frac{n^3}{n^2 - n + 1} \right\rfloor = n$.
This establishes $a_n = n$ for all odd $n \ge 3$.
Checking $n=1$ trivially satisfies $a_1 = 1$.
Since $n=999$ is odd and $999 \ge 3$, it follows that $a_{999} = 999$.
